content.title: About
content.content: Aloe vera juice drink is a refreshing non‑alcoholic beverage made from the juice of aloe vera leaves, water, a small amount of sugar or sweeteners, and sometimes fruit flavorings. It is rich in vitamins, minerals, and biologically active compounds characteristic of the aloe plant.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Aloe vera has been used in traditional medicine for over 6,000 years.
The leaf juice contains more than 200 bioactive compounds, including polysaccharides, glycoproteins, and anthraquinones.
Commercial drinks are often fortified with vitamin C and B12 for added immune support.
Aloe can be grown at home, but extracting a clean juice requires special processing of the leaves.
In some countries the product is sold as a concentrate that is diluted with water before consumption.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Polysaccharides and glycoproteins in aloe help balance gut microbiota and relieve constipation.

items.title: Antioxidant effect
items.content: Vitamins A, C, E and enzymes in the drink help neutralize free radicals.

items.title: Immune system boost
items.content: Bioactive compounds stimulate immune cell activity and increase resistance to infections.

items.title: Skin hydration
items.content: Regular consumption contributes to better skin hydration from the inside out.

items.title: Blood sugar regulation
items.content: Some studies suggest aloe may improve insulin sensitivity.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions such as rash or itching.

items.title: Anthraquinone content
items.content: High doses of anthraquinones can be toxic, so recommended serving sizes should be followed.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Aloe may enhance the effects of diuretics and blood‑glucose‑lowering medications.

items.title: Pregnancy and lactation
items.content: Pregnant or nursing women should consult a healthcare professional before drinking.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Consume the drink chilled, typically 200–250 ml per day. It can be added to smoothies, mocktails, or used as a base for non‑alcoholic mixes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and use within 7 days. Discard if the smell or taste changes.

frozen-coffee-drink-decaffeinated-with-n.title: Frozen Coffee Drink, Decaffeinated, with Non-Dairy Milk and Whipped Cream

content.title: About
content.content: The frozen coffee drink, decaffeinated, with non-dairy milk and whipped cream is a refreshing beverage made from ground coffee that has undergone decaffeination, blended with a light plant‑based milk (such as oat or almond) and topped with a airy, dairy‑free whipped topping. Served as a frozen frothy treat similar to a frappe, it is suitable for those avoiding caffeine and dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination retains most of the original coffee flavor while removing almost all caffeine.
Plant milks like oat, almond or soy give the drink a smooth texture and a subtle natural sweetness.
Vegan whipped cream is often made from coconut cream or other plant‑based creams, making it suitable for vegans.
Frozen coffee beverages are a staple of summer menus worldwide, especially in hot climates.
Sugar levels can be adjusted—from completely unsweetened to a sweetened version according to taste.

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: Decaffeinated coffee provides the aroma and taste without the stimulating effect of caffeine, which is ideal for caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of plant protein and vitamins
items.content: Non‑dairy milk adds a modest amount of protein, B‑vitamins, and calcium, especially when fortified.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Certain plant milks (e.g., oat) contain soluble fiber that can aid normal digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie dessert option
items.content: When made with limited sweetener and without heavy cream, the drink can be a light treat with moderate calories.

items.title: Allergy to plant ingredients
items.content: Some people may be allergic to nuts, soy, or oats used in the plant milk.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened versions may contain significant sugar, which is undesirable for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Coffee acidity
items.content: Even without caffeine, coffee remains acidic and may irritate the stomach of people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Commercial products may contain stabilizers and emulsifiers that are not suitable for all consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the frozen coffee in a glass or cup, garnish with an extra swirl of dairy‑free whipped topping, and optionally dust with cinnamon or cocoa powder. Add a splash of flavored syrup (vanilla, caramel, etc.) for extra sweetness if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared drink in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. For longer storage (over two weeks) sugar may crystallize, so it is best consumed within a week.

rice-white-with-carrots-and-tomatoes-and.title: White Rice with Carrots and Tomatoes and/or Tomato‑Based Sauce, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: This dish consists of boiled white rice, carrots and tomatoes, and may include a tomato‑based sauce. No fat is added, making it low‑calorie and suitable for diet nutrition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is a staple source of carbohydrates in many countries.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Tomatoes contain lycopene – a powerful antioxidant that helps protect cells.
A fat‑free tomato sauce retains most of the beneficial compounds while delivering a bright flavor.
The dish can be adapted to various cuisines by adding spices, herbs, or swapping the sauce for vegetable broth.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rice provides a quick source of energy through easily digestible carbohydrates.

items.title: Vision support
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots is converted to vitamin A, essential for eye health.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Lycopene from tomatoes helps neutralize free radicals and may reduce the risk of certain chronic diseases.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes the dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets and weight management.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice contains thiamine, niacin, and vitamin B6, which support carbohydrate metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Unlike whole grains, white rice provides little dietary fiber, which may affect digestion.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or tomato sauce.

items.title: Sodium in sauce
items.content: Fat‑free tomato sauce often contains salt; those watching sodium intake should choose a low‑salt version.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot as a main course or as a side to meat, fish, or legumes. Add fresh herbs, spices (paprika, turmeric) or a splash of lemon juice to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cooked rice can be stored in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 3‑4 days. Keep vegetables and sauce separate to prevent sogginess. When reheating, add a small amount of water to restore moisture.

content.title: About
content.content: Spaghetti sauce with poultry (1220) is a ready‑to‑use tomato sauce enriched with pieces of cooked chicken breast and aromatic herbs. It is designed for quick pasta preparation, delivering a rich tomato flavor, mild spiciness, and a subtle meaty aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sauce blends a classic Italian tomato base with chicken meat, making it more protein‑rich than typical vegetarian sauces.
Dried basil, oregano and garlic are used to give it a distinctive Mediterranean scent.
The product is packaged in a glass jar, preserving taste and aroma without added preservatives.
Besides spaghetti, the sauce works well as a base for lasagna, ragù, and casseroles.

items.title: High‑quality protein source
items.content: Chicken pieces provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Lycopene in tomatoes
items.content: Tomatoes contain lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that supports heart health and may reduce the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sauce supplies vitamins B6 and B12, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Unlike cream‑based sauces, this product has low saturated‑fat content, making it suitable for lighter diets.

items.title: Iron source
items.content: Chicken and tomatoes together provide a modest amount of iron, beneficial for blood formation.

items.title: Chicken allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to poultry should avoid this sauce.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The sauce contains a moderate amount of salt; those monitoring sodium intake should account for it.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate
items.content: Some batches may include MSG as a flavor enhancer; sensitive individuals should be aware.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Heat the sauce in a saucepan, add cooked spaghetti and stir. Optionally top with grated Parmesan, fresh basil, or a drizzle of olive oil. The sauce also works for casseroles, layered dishes, and as a pizza base.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.

content.title: About
content.content: Swiss chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris) is a leafy green vegetable with large, glossy leaves and thick, crunchy stalks. The stalks can be white, yellow, orange, pink, or red, and the leaves taste mildly earthy and slightly bitter. It is eaten cooked in soups, sautés, pies, and stuffed dishes, and the young leaves can be used raw in salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Swiss chard belongs to the same species as beets, but it is grown for its leaves and stalks rather than its root.
Despite the name, chard is thought to have originated in the Mediterranean region, not in Switzerland.
Rainbow chard has brightly colored stalks in several hues.
Both leaves and stalks are edible, though stalks take longer to cook.
Chard has been used in Mediterranean cooking for centuries.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Swiss chard is an excellent source of vitamin K, which supports normal blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Provides vitamins A and C
items.content: It contains carotenoids that the body can convert into vitamin A, and vitamin C.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Swiss chard provides magnesium, potassium, and iron.

items.title: Contains plant pigments
items.content: Its colorful stalks contain betalains and flavonoids, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Swiss chard is low in calories and provides fiber and volume to meals.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Swiss chard is high in oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stones in susceptible people and may reduce calcium and iron absorption.

items.title: Possible medication interactions
items.content: Swiss chard contains vitamin K. People taking blood thinners should consult a healthcare professional about keeping their intake consistent.

items.title: Potassium and sodium
items.content: Swiss chard is relatively high in potassium and naturally contains some sodium, which matters for people on restricted diets.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Raw leafy greens can carry bacteria, so wash them thoroughly before eating.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Swiss chard can be sautéed with garlic and olive oil, steamed, added to soups, stews, frittatas, and pasta, or used instead of cabbage leaves for stuffing. Chop the stalks and cook them a few minutes longer than the leaves. Young leaves can be eaten raw in salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unwashed Swiss chard in the refrigerator in a loosely closed bag or container, where it usually keeps for three to five days. Wash it right before use. It can also be blanched and frozen.
